title: Alkaline Phosphatase
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Measures alkaline phosphatase, an enzyme in the blood. It is often used to screen for or help diagnose liver or bone diseases.
low: A low ALP is less common. It may point to zinc or protein deficiency, malnutrition, pernicious anemia, thyroid disease, Wilson disease, or hypophosphatasia, a rare genetic disease affecting bones and teeth.
high: From the liver, a high level may follow bile duct blockages, cirrhosis, hepatitis or mononucleosis. If liver tests are normal, a bone disorder such as Paget's disease of bone may be the source. Moderately high levels are also listed with Hodgkin lymphoma, heart failure and certain infections.
notes: The test alone cannot show which source is causing a high level, so other tests are usually needed. Pregnancy, growth in children and teenagers, birth control pills, some medicines and a fatty meal before testing can all affect results.
